incomePathways.rationale: Same-household NET consumption/after-tax work jointly logged with full incremental access/time costs relative to self/county application. Positive overlap never discounts negative costs. Federal payer incidence is a separate geographic choice.
incomePathways.counterfactual: County/self-application, other navigators/partners and existing federal school-meal programs. SNAP money is a transfer: recipients and distinct public payers both assessed.

current.assumptions: FullFY2025 recipient cost against a conditional SNAP-navigation channel; native applications not approvals. Local recipient welfare plus separately assessed global public-payer losses; this partial boundary omits otherstate recipient gains. School policy is a standalone finite sensitivity, never additive to overlapping SNAP households. All causal/resource/utility/geographic coefficients judged, not empirical HFC EV.

why: Clinical health now requires SNAP receipt; corresponding Denver-transfer global payer losses remain fully counted.
